On $[0,1]$, take the open-in-the-subspace cover
$U=(-1,\tfrac34)\cap[0,1]$ and $V=(\tfrac14,2)\cap[0,1]$. Define
$$\varphi(x)=\max\{0,\min\{1,2-3x\}\},\qquad\psi(x)=1-\varphi(x).$$
Then $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are continuous, nonnegative, and sum to one. Their
supports are contained respectively in $[0,\tfrac23]\subseteq U$ and
$[\tfrac13,1]\subseteq V$, so they are a finite subordinate partition of unity.
explanation: The clipped affine function equals one through x=1/3, decreases linearly to zero at x=2/3, and stays zero thereafter. Thus the two supports are [0,2/3] and [1/3,1], contained strictly in their assigned cover members. This direct pair needs no choice; the final comparison explicitly respects the existence theorem hypotheses.

$\varphi_n(x)=\psi(x-n)$. The functions are continuous, take values in

$U_n=(n-\tfrac32,n+\tfrac32)$ of $\mathbb R$.
explanation: For x in [n,n+1], only the two neighboring hats can be nonzero, and their displayed values sum to one. At integer endpoints one hat has value one and the other zero. Bounded neighborhoods meet finitely many integer-indexed supports, proving local finiteness and correct subordination.

exact_passage:
In $\mathbb R$, let $I_n=(1/(n+1),1/n)$ for positive integers $n$. The intervals
are pairwise disjoint, so no point lies in two intervals and the family is
point-finite. Every neighbourhood of $0$, however, meets $I_n$ for all
sufficiently large $n$. Therefore the family is not locally finite at $0$.
explanation: The intervals are disjoint, but every neighborhood of zero meets their tail. Point finiteness and failure of local finiteness follow directly from the stated definitions.

countably compact, and noncompact by
[[thm-ordinal-spaces-and-compactness]] and

[[lem-countably-compact-paracompact-hausdorff-is-compact]] would make it compact.
It is therefore not paracompact.
explanation: All premises are supplied under AC: omega1 is Hausdorff, countably compact, and noncompact. AC implies countable choice, so the compactness consequence of paracompactness applies and gives the stated contradiction.
